note: Inputs on which the current injector has been through the full gate ladder of docs/QA_ACCEPTANCE_STANDARD.md. Only sha256 is stored - no ROM is distributed. Add an entry only after runtime + behaviour + visual QA on that exact input hash. Each entry carries font_gate: "entered" means the runtime CJK-font gate measured a real Chinese face on that host and Chinese mode opens; "refused" means the adapter installs, measures, finds no face, and hands the key back, so the ROM keeps its stock keyboard and never renders Latin stand-ins for Hanzi. Both classes are validated; neither claim is inferred from the other, and each entry names the capture that proves it.

hosts.note: Behaviour proof on the exact patched bytes: lock word C000 after the grid is reached, name buffer 010001000100FFFF after three CN presses, lock back to 0000 after SELECT; the same-route control on the unpatched input shows none of these. Runtime font gate: ENTERED, so the adapter measured a real CJK face in this host before letting Chinese mode open. Visual gate: screenshots in the patched evidence dir show the 4x8 grid overlay, cursor alignment and the Chinese/stock transition. Whether the cells render real Hanzi depends on this host carrying a CJK font - the payload ships no glyph tiles - and is graded A/B by hand in test_roms/README.md section 15; this entry does not claim either way. Gate 4's exhaustive boundary list is also run per host (27 steps: R/L page change, 223<->0 wrap, Page-Tab unlock, pair-vs-Latin delete discriminator, mixed-buffer overflow rejection) and the entry is refused unless tools/check_boundary_route.py passes it against these same bytes. That route's locked-grid frame is byte-identical to the grid frame named above, so the visual gate covers both routes rather than needing 27 more sign-offs per host (re-measured by tools/grid_frame_equivalence.py). Recorded 2026-09-27 by tools/record_validated_hosts.py.

Runtime font gate: REFUSED. This host's own font has no CJK face, so the adapter installs, measures the page it would have drawn, and hands the key back to the stock page swap - the ROM is playable with its original keyboard and never shows Latin stand-ins for Hanzi. Proof on the exact patched bytes: the probe capture log is byte-identical to the same-route control on the unpatched input (run6_patched vs run6_clean), neither contains a Chinese lock word (C000/C001/C0DF), and tools/check_refusal_pixels.py reports 0 novel pixels across every sampled frame of both routes, i.e. the refusal draws ink the stock ROM cannot show nowhere. Gate 4's 27-step boundary list is run per host and is graded for a refusal here - patched must equal its own control step for step - which tools/check_boundary_route.py asserts against these same bytes. excluded.why: gate-4 boundary route does not pass: ROUTE GAP: sNamingScreen is 00000000 at b01, outside EWRAM - this host needs its own nav route
excluded.reason: The naming screen is not in this build's reachable flow: the demo opens after name entry, with the protagonist already named (opening text hardcodes 'Charlie loves rats', the START menu's second row is 'Charlie', and a full-ROM search for the stock naming prompts returns 0 hits -- see test_roms/README.md section 15.7). Re-proven on the current bytes by diag_card/png/k020_card.png, the trainer card (NAME: Charlie, IDNo.43902) captured on this exact patched ROM with its own artifact.txt; sNamingScreen reads 00000000 while that card is on screen, so the pointer is not being read at the wrong address. The patch is also measured inert here: boundary_final_patched/ and boundary_final_clean/ replay the same script on the patched and unpatched ROM against the same emulator build (both artifact.txt carry the same harness= hash) and their 27 PNGs are byte-identical. Hence ROUTE GAP at b01, not a behaviour failure: this host has no name-entry screen to take over, which is out of scope for CKI and is not a claim that the ROM is incompatible.

known_limitations.decision: 两条都按已记录缺陷发货：链塌缩那 3 台记为已知限制；退出缺陷现在不修。
known_limitations.meaning: Both ship as documented limitations instead of being fixed in this release. Each one already has independent evidence that the *outcome* is right; what is missing is attribution (limitation 1) or one frame of cosmetics (limitation 2). Neither fix is a measurement - both need a payload change, and a payload change re-records all 25 hosts on both compiler routes and reopens the visual sign-off.

limitations.what: The gate finds its button sprite through host bytes (ns[0x1E24] -> gSprites[fid][0x3C]). On these three the chain collapses onto one sprite (fid == bid == 0), so the gate's three words sit in host-owned gSprites[0].data[] and its state cannot be attributed after the fact - tools/read_gate_verdict.py reports them as unattributable rather than guessing.
limitations.why_shippable: The outcome of each is proven by other evidence, not by this readout: the two entered hosts by lock word C000 + the three double-byte chars in the name buffer + signed-off screenshots, the refused one by a probe capture log byte-identical to its own control and check_refusal_pixels.py reporting 0 novel pixels. Writing into that sprite has shown no visible effect on either route.
limitations.cost_to_fix: Any other landing site for the three words is still somebody's data[] (the payload has no writable statics), so the change needs a new proven-unused slot plus a full re-record: 25 hosts x 2 routes, behaviour + boundary + visual gates.

limitations.what: SELECT and the PAGE tab clear the lock flag without repainting the keyboard, so the Chinese grid stays on screen until the host's next page swap repaints it.
limitations.why_shippable: Names, lock words and the cursor are all correct at the moment of unlock; only the picture lags by one page swap, and the stock renderer overwrites it. Both paths were exercised and behave the same way.
limitations.cost_to_fix: One call per path in payload/adapter_v10.c: the ck_handle_frame SELECT branch (line 1130 at the time of writing) and the ck_page_handler unlock branch (line 1147). Either is a payload change, so it re-records all 25 hosts on both routes.
